title: skyBlip companion link registry (v1)
description: Every frame on the companion link's config and log endpoints, and the number each of its keys travels under. A frame is one CBOR map (RFC 8949) in one write or one notification, in one grammar every reader of the link holds to: the map's keys unsigned and ascending, every head in its shortest form and its argument within 32 bits, definite lengths only, no floats, no tags, no null, and nothing nested but an array of unsigned integers. Text is UTF-8: the firmware writes nothing else and every reader refuses a malformed sequence. link.v1.vectors.json holds what the readers refuse and what the clients' encoders refuse, and the firmware, blip.py and the server each test against it. Key 0 is 'command' in every frame and is not listed under 'keys': its value is the 'code' of a frame below, which says which frame this is and therefore which key table applies. A frame's 'keys' list every other key it may carry, each with its 'name' (what a client shows and accepts), its 'number', assigned once and never reused within the frame, and its 'type': 'unsigned' and 'integer' (a CBOR unsigned or negative integer; 'unsigned' is never negative), 'boolean', 'text' (UTF-8, only for free text a person reads or types), 'bytes' (a byte string, never hex or base64; 'bytes' with a number is its fixed length), 'unsigned_array' (an array of unsigned integers) and 'enum' (an unsigned integer whose names are the values of the enum named by 'enum'). Every frame and every key has a 'description': what it means, when it is present and the range it takes. A key with 'required' true is in every frame of its command that carries keys: the unit's answer where the host asks with the bare command, the host's own frame where only the host sends one. A frame with 'keys_of' shares the key table of the frame it names, so the same key is the same number in both: 'set', 'config' and 'defaults' are one table, so a 'defaults' reply with its command swapped is a 'set', and 'radio' is the radio group of 'diagnostics'. 'endpoint' is the characteristic it travels on, 'sender' who writes it: 'host' (a page, blip.py), 'unit', or 'both' when the host asks with the bare command and the unit answers under the same one. Under 'enums', each value has a 'name' and a 'code'; 'mirrors' names the C++ enum whose numbering the codes are and, under 'off_the_wire', the enumerators the link never carries, and a value's 'mirrors' its enumerator. firmware/test/core/test_link_mirrors.cpp holds them to it both ways: each code to its enumerator, and the enum to the registry through a switch over every value named here, which -Wswitch refuses to compile once the C++ enum gains one the registry lacks. firmware/core/comms/README.md says how the link carries them, and schemas/activation.v1.schema.json what the activation signatures cover and the JSON the browser posts to the server. scripts/link_registry.py generates firmware/core/comms/link_registry.h, firmware/simulator/world/link_names.h, firmware/test/core/test_link_mirrors.cpp and server/app/javascript/skyblip/link_registry.js from this file, and scripts/check_link_registry.py fails when one of them differs from what it would write, when a frame or a key has no description, and when firmware/core/comms/config_reports.cpp writes the status frame other than its keys say. scripts/blip_frames.py, which scripts/blip.py speaks through, reads this file directly.

frames.description: Unit to host on the config endpoint: the verdict on a command that has no reply of its own, a refusal of any command, or a prompt standing on the glass. 11 bytes at its widest, so every link carries it.

keys.name: acknowledge
keys.description: The command was carried out. False is a refusal, or a prompt waiting on the glass when pending is true

keys.name: pending
keys.description: A prompt stands on the glass under the word in reason: two presses answer it with the command's verdict, one press answers cancelled, thirty seconds expired, and the asking link dropping takes it

keys.name: reason
keys.description: The word for the verdict, the refusal or the prompt, from the one enumeration every frame shares (firmware/core/comms/README.md and server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md say which command answers which)

keys.name: by
keys.description: On a claimed refusal, the session that holds the claim: one central at a time commands the unit (firmware/core/comms/README.md, The claim)

frames.description: Host to unit: asks for the stored settings, answered under command config.

Unit to host, the answer to get: the settings a companion app reads, one CBOR map in one frame. config, set and defaults share this key table. Every key here is read by the firmware: settings with no reader were removed rather than accepted and ignored (region, rotation, power_save, dropped after v1.0; page_mask, dropped when the pad's walk became three pages nothing may hide; stealth and gyro, dropped with the features themselves). Every key but the two per-unit bench trims (battery_offset_mv, frequency_trim_e1_ppm) is returned, 31 bytes at the widest. The radar's range and plot are stored settings with no key here: they are set on the device's own menu, and the link neither shows nor sets them. A key with no reading behind it is absent, never a zero.

keys.name: version
keys.description: The settings contract, always 1 in a config reply and absent from defaults. It moves when a key changes meaning, not when the flash layout does (products/skyblip_go/settings.h, kCurrentVersion)

keys.name: address
keys.description: The 24-bit ADS-L address this unit transmits under, read-only: manufacturer prefix 0x00 followed by the 16-bit serial skyblip.eu assigned from 1 and signed at activation (activation.v1.schema.json). Absent until the unit is activated, as any key with no reading behind it is: a unit with no serial has no address and neither transmits nor receives, so a page reads 'address' in the reply as activated. Not a stored setting: the unit re-verifies its unlock code at every boot, so a 'set' carrying this key is ignored like any key with no reader

keys.name: address_mapping_table
keys.description: ADS-L address mapping table (issue 2 F.2.2), 0 to 63: 0=random/privacy, 1-4 reserved, 5=ICAO, 6=FLARM, 7=OGN-Tracker, 8=FANET, 9+ manufacturer pages, each a registry-assigned 8-bit prefix and a 16-bit base address. A constant 58 on this device, manufacturer page 49 with prefix 0x00 as the ADS-L registry assigned it, so address is that prefix and the unit's serial. Present whether or not the unit is activated, read-only like address.

keys.name: aircraft_type
keys.description: ADS-L aircraft category, 0 to 17

keys.name: alarm_enabled
keys.description: The traffic alarm sounds. False silences the buzzer and the haptic both, as alarm_volume off does

keys.name: alarm_volume
keys.description: The three steps of the radar menu's VOLUME row. Off silences the buzzer and the haptic both, as 'alarm_enabled' false does. Soft and loud pulse the haptic with each call. A device ships on loud. Firmware before this scale took 0 to 5, where 3 and up all drove the piezo at the same duty; a stored value comes back as 0 off, 1 and 2 soft, 3 to 5 loud

keys.name: units
keys.description: nautical (NM, kt) or metric (km, km/h): the aeronautical unit is the first one because it is the one a pilot flies, and a device ships on it. Decides every page that prints a distance or a speed: the radar's range ring, the nearby page's distance column, the six-pack's speed dial. Altitudes and vertical speeds stay in feet whatever this says, and the status page shows the aeronautical figure and the SI one side by side

keys.name: callsign
keys.description: Upper-case letters, digits, dash and blank, the characters the radar menu types and the ones a $PFLAA ID field can carry, and the aircraft's registration as the radio says it. Set on the radar menu or over this link, shown on the status page, reported back here, and transmitted once every ten seconds: ADS-L's own Traffic payload carries no name, so it goes out under payload type 66, the entry F.2.1 assigns to OGN and whose definition it leaves to them (TelemType 1, InfoType 5, 14 characters). Empty means nothing is transmitted, which is the default and the privacy answer: an address a receiver cannot resolve stays anonymous, and a registration in clear does not. Nine characters here against the wire's fourteen, because that is what the stored settings blob has always held

keys.name: battery_offset_mv
keys.description: From -250 to 250. Per-unit battery gauge trim in millivolts, added to every reading before a state of charge or a cutoff is read into it. Set once on the production line against a bench supply: two 1% divider resistors put the ratio out by up to 2% (84 mV at a full cell) and the SAADC's gain and reference error adds to that, on a curve whose flat middle spends 250 mV crossing 60 percentage points. The bound is three times the divider's own worst case; beyond it the unit is wired wrong, not out of trim. Write-only over the link: set on the line, it is read back as the millivolts the status reply and the panel already show

keys.name: frequency_trim_e1_ppm
keys.description: From -100 to 100. Radio centre-frequency trim in tenths of a ppm, positive upwards, applied to every dwell the SX1262 arms (receive and transmit alike). The board fits a TCXO, so 0 is the design intent and the expected value on every unit; the field exists because nothing on the device can measure the reference, and a batch of TCXOs ten times worse than its datasheet would otherwise be a recall. The bound is that tenfold miss (+-10 ppm, +-8.7 kHz at 868.2 MHz): inside it the carrier cannot leave ERC 70-03 band h1.4 (868.0-868.6 MHz), beyond it the part is broken rather than out of trim. Set only against a spectrum analyser or a frequency counter. Write-only over the link, like battery_offset_mv: the device has nothing that could measure the value back for itself.

frames.description: Asked with the bare command, answered under defaults with the keys of config a pilot can set, as a new unit ships them: no version and no address keys, so the reply with its command swapped for set puts a unit back on its defaults. The per-unit trims and the radar's range and plot are not in it and are left as they are.

Host to unit: the keys of config to change, every one accepted, the others left as stored. The unit asks on its glass under confirm, and two presses store them and answer a bare acknowledgement, on the ground only.

Asked with the bare command, and the one frame the unit also sends without being asked: while a link is up, a change of flight state, a charging flip, a change of power level or a five-percent step of the state of charge pushes it to every subscribed central. With every key at its widest it is 20 bytes, the payload every link guarantees, pinned byte for byte in firmware/test/products/test_comms_report.cpp. It carries what a pilot's screen shows and nothing a bench reads: why the device came up is reset and whether a gauge is fitted is battery_valid in diagnostics, the address and the callsign are config's. A key with no reading behind it is absent, never a zero. The firmware writes the keys in ascending number, and scripts/check_link_registry.py holds firmware/core/comms/config_reports.cpp to this table: the keys, their order, their types and which may be absent.

keys.name: flight
keys.description: The confirmed flight state. Every settings change and upload is refused unless this reads ground, so 'unknown' refuses too

keys.name: upload
keys.description: A firmware upload window is open: granted by the confirmation gesture on the device, true only on the ground, closed for good by a takeoff

keys.name: battery_percent
keys.description: 0 to 100. State of charge, 0 where the device takes itself down rather than where a datasheet calls the cell empty, read on the discharge curve. ABSENT until the gauge has a reading of the cell, for ever on a board with no divider, and while the cable is in, because the divider reads the USB rail there and not the cell

keys.name: charging
keys.description: The cable is in. No pin says when the charge ends, so a full cell on the cable still reads true

keys.name: power_level
keys.description: What core/power's cutoff rule made of the same samples, three consecutive readings to step down and three to step back up. low is the cell past the knee, about 12%: the device asks for a charger and refuses nothing. critical, about 5%, refuses every durable write but the flight record. flat is the device taking itself down. unknown: no believable reading yet. The glass and the USB console print OK, LOW, CRITICAL, FLAT and --

keys.name: went_dark_flat
keys.description: The last time this unit went dark it was for a flat cell: the cutoff took it down, or a switch-on was refused below the boot lockout. The glass says FLAT BATTERY until a charger wakes the unit, and this outlives that frame: true for the whole of the one boot that followed, false from the boot after. The self-test page prints the same fact as WAS FLAT

keys.name: die_temperature_c
keys.description: From -50 to 125. Die temperature in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. ABSENT rather than zero when no reading younger than 30 seconds exists, because 0.0 C is a plausible hangar morning. Same key and same value as diagnostics'.

frames.description: The bench's slot timing report, asked with the bare command (core/timing/slot_timing_statistics.h): the PPS and dwell histograms and the executor's switching figures, since boot. One frame on a 182-byte link, 147 bytes at its widest, and consecutive parts on a narrower one. Refused no_statistics where no accumulator is wired.

keys.name: part
keys.description: Frame index within one answer, from 0

keys.name: more
keys.description: Another frame follows. Exactly one frame per answer carries false

keys.name: pps_us
keys.description: Counts of PPS interval errors in seven buckets, signed and symmetric about zero, edged at kRetuneUs, kHopGuardUs and kJitterGuardUs. An error past the widest edge saturates into the outermost bucket

keys.name: pps_worst_us
keys.description: The largest PPS interval error since boot, signed, in microseconds

keys.name: pps_samples
keys.description: PPS intervals counted in pps_us

keys.name: dwell_us
keys.description: Counts of dwell phase errors, from the armed instant to the burst keying, in the seven buckets of pps_us

keys.name: dwell_worst_us
keys.description: The largest dwell phase error since boot, signed, in microseconds

keys.name: dwell_samples
keys.description: Dwell phases counted in dwell_us

keys.name: holdover_events
keys.description: PPS gaps longer than 1.5 s, at least one edge missing, which is holdover and not a sample for pps_us

keys.name: missed
keys.description: Dwells that carried a plan and closed without the outcome they were armed for

keys.name: refused
keys.description: Plans never armed because the hour's air-time budget was spent (core/timing/transmit.h)

keys.name: switch_hop_us
keys.description: The executor's slowest M-band channel hop since boot, in microseconds, the figure the hop guard is sized from

keys.name: switch_to_o_band_us
keys.description: The executor's slowest change from the M band to the O band since boot, in microseconds

keys.name: switch_to_m_band_us
keys.description: The executor's slowest change from the O band back to the M band since boot, in microseconds

keys.name: late_dwells
keys.description: Dwells armed ahead that were still not listening at their start

frames.description: The durable-write window's bench figures, asked with the bare command (core/timing/durable_write.h): how the settings writes were placed against the radio's dwells since boot. Refused no_statistics where no window is wired.

keys.name: writable
keys.description: The power rule allows a settings write now (core/power/cutoff.h)

keys.name: requests
keys.description: Changes that asked for a durable write since boot

keys.name: writes
keys.description: Writes those changes cost: requests over writes is the coalescing ratio

keys.name: forced
keys.description: Writes that could not be placed outside a dwell inside the bound and were forced

keys.name: worst_wait_ms
keys.description: The longest a change waited for its write, from the oldest unwritten change

keys.name: pending
keys.description: A change is waiting for its write now

keys.name: budget_ms
keys.description: kWorstWriteMs, the longest one settings write may take, which a placed write keeps clear of the next dwell

keys.name: bound_ms
keys.description: kDeferCeilingMs, the longest a change may wait before its write is forced

frames.description: Asked with the bare command: the radio group of diagnostics alone, answered under radio with the keys of diagnostics. Unlike the whole dump it is answered before a dump has been collected, since a radio that has heard nothing truthfully has zero receptions.

One dump, two surfaces, one table behind both (firmware/core/comms/diagnostics.h). Asked with the bare command and answered as one frame per subsystem, or more where the negotiated payload cannot carry a subsystem whole: every frame carries group, part and more, no frame mixes two groups, and no frame exceeds the payload the asking central negotiated. Over USB CDC the same table is printed every ten seconds as one line per subsystem, '<group> key=value key="text value" ...', with the same group names, keys and values, an enumeration printed as the words the glass uses (reset="CPU LOCKUP" where the link carries lockup): a laptop on the bench and a phone on the wing must not report a device differently. Asking for the whole dump before the device has collected one is refused no_statistics, since a device must not report health it has not measured. Nothing here is reset by being read. Each key's description starts with the group it belongs to. The widest group, the radio's, is 112 bytes.

keys.name: group
keys.description: The subsystem every field in this frame belongs to. One console line per group, in this order.

keys.name: part
keys.description: Frame index within one answer, from 0. A group that does not fit the negotiated payload spans consecutive parts

keys.name: more
keys.description: Another frame follows. Exactly one frame per answer carries false

keys.name: uptime_s
keys.description: system. Seconds since boot, from hal::Clock::millis(). Wraps with the 32-bit millisecond counter at 49.7 days.

keys.name: reset
keys.description: system. Why the device came up (core/power/reset_reason.h). The console prints the words core/power/reset_reason.cpp spells: UNKNOWN, POWER ON, RESET PIN, BROWNOUT, SOFT RESET, WATCHDOG, CPU LOCKUP, CHARGER WAKE, BUTTON WAKE, DEBUGGER

keys.name: link_drops
keys.description: system. Frames the companion link could not send: over the negotiated payload, refused by the controller, or left incomplete by a writer. Silence towards a phone is a fault worth a number

keys.name: noise_dbm
keys.description: radio. The measured noise floor, core/timing::NoiseFloor, in dBm, from -128 to 127. A diagnostic and nothing else: nothing on this device defers a burst to what it hears, so a loud site is reported rather than transmitted around (firmware/core/timing/README.md)

keys.name: duty_permille
keys.description: radio. Parts per thousand, 0 to 1000, of the transmit allowance spent over the hour's sliding window (EN 300 220-2 V3.3.1 Table 4 band M, 1%). The declared channel-access route, and the only rule that refuses a burst

keys.name: rx_ok
keys.description: radio. Frames received and decoded

keys.name: rx_bad
keys.description: radio. Receptions that are a fault: a frame that framed, was attempted and was refused, plus the integrity failures an error correction could not rescue. Not a burst nothing was attempted on (rx_wait), not a message type this firmware does not implement (rx_type), not a burst that named no system at all (rx_unframed), not a frame keyed on a second we disagree with (rx_miskeyed), and not a transmission of ours that never completed (tx_lost)

keys.name: rx_wait
keys.description: radio. Frames no decode was attempted on, because an ALP-TAS position is coded relative to the receiver and keyed on the UTC second, so it needs a fix and a date of our own. Climbs on a device still acquiring next to a transmitting neighbour, which is correct behaviour and not a failure

keys.name: rx_type
keys.description: radio. Frames that framed and carried a message type this firmware does not implement: ALP-TAS reads its 2024 position frame and nothing else, so a SoftRF interleaving Air V6 with Air V7 lands here. The neighbour's dialect, not our failure

keys.name: rx_unframed
keys.description: radio. Bursts that held the shared sync window and decoded too cleanly to be noise, but whose sync tail named neither M-band system. A neighbour on another dialect, or a receiver framing at the wrong offset: either way not a frame this firmware refused

keys.name: rx_miskeyed
keys.description: radio. ALP-TAS frames whose CRC held and whose sender keyed them on a second inside 18 s of ours but not ours: the key stage moves every 16 s and the frame carries the low 4 bits of its own second, so a clock disagreement is reported as the offset it is rather than as a decode failure. Climbing here means one of the two clocks is wrong, not the radio

keys.name: rx_noise
keys.description: radio. What the band's own noise framed: a sync window that filled with something carrying no frame at all. The floor under every other reception counter, and the one that tells a deaf receiver from an empty sky

keys.name: rx_named
keys.description: radio. Bursts that framed and carried an aircraft's registration instead of its position: ADS-L payload 66, OGN's, read for the callsign and filed under the sender's address (core/radio/README.md, radio::Verdict::Named). Counted apart from rx_ok, which counts positions

keys.name: tx_ok
keys.description: radio. Bursts the executor reported as transmitted

keys.name: tx_lost
keys.description: radio. Bursts of ours that were armed and never completed: the dwell ran out, or the radio's transmit timeout did. Never a reception

keys.name: tx_named
keys.description: radio. How many of the bursts in tx_ok carried own-ship's registration rather than a position: the callsign goes on the air once every ten seconds, in slot 1's tail (core/timing/README.md)

keys.name: tx_keyed_us
keys.description: radio. Microseconds the last burst held the carrier keyed, measured by the executor rather than budgeted

keys.name: tx_span_us
keys.description: radio. Microseconds from arming the last burst to the radio reporting it sent, which is the keyed time plus everything around it

keys.name: range_refused
keys.description: radio. Receptions core/traffic refused because the position they claimed was further away than this radio can hear (core/traffic/sanity.h). A rate that climbs is a receiver at the edge of its link budget or a decoder that is silently miscorrecting

keys.name: dio1_armed
keys.description: radio. The executor holds a rising-edge interrupt on the SX1262's DIO1 and sleeps on it between events. False on the host executor, which has no interrupt line, and on silicon when the GPIO driver refused the trigger: the executor then reads DIO1 every 200 us instead

keys.name: dio1_edges
keys.description: radio. DIO1 rising edges the interrupt handler saw since boot. Near rx and tx events combined on a healthy line; zero with dio1_armed true is a trigger that never fires

keys.name: dio1_missed
keys.description: radio. Events a status read found while DIO1 still read low: a TxDone read in the tail of a burst, the 4 ms safety poll, or the drain at a dwell's end. Rising with tx_ok means DIO1 trails TxDone, rising with rx_ok means it trails RxDone too

keys.name: tracked
keys.description: traffic. Aircraft currently in the table, after ageing out, at most 48

keys.name: alarm
keys.description: traffic. The alarm level standing right now: 0 none, 1 info, 2 important, 3 urgent

keys.name: fixes
keys.description: gnss. Solutions the own-ship service has accepted since boot. Zero on a device whose receiver is wired but silent

keys.name: valid
keys.description: gnss. Whether own-ship currently holds a valid fix

keys.name: baud
keys.description: gnss. The rate we are ACTUALLY talking to the receiver at, which is the devicetree's rate until autobaud had to move. A receiver silently at another rate is a GNSS-less device that looks fitted

keys.name: config
keys.description: gnss. Where the receiver's configuration sequence stands (ports::GnssConfigStage, run by hardware/parts/l76k): idle before it starts, restarting, waking, identifying by the $PCAS06 banner, sending the $PCAS sentences, verifying that the receiver obeys them, confirming while a raised port rate waits for its first sentence, then ready; degraded once three verifications failed with no other rate left to try. The console prints IDLE, RESTART, WAKING, IDENT, SENDING, VERIFY, CONFIRM, READY and DEGRADED

keys.name: raises
keys.description: gnss. Times the driver asked the receiver to move to 115200 baud with $PCAS01, which it does only after the receiver passed verification and only on a port that can retune (core/gnss/README.md)

keys.name: raise_fallbacks
keys.description: gnss. Raises after which no sentence checksummed at the new rate inside the 3 s verify window, so the port went back to the rate before: a receiver that ignored $PCAS01, which never acknowledges

keys.name: solution_phase_ms
keys.description: gnss. Milliseconds after the latched PPS edge at which own-ship last published a solution, modulo 1000 (products/skyblip_go/services/ownship.cpp). A solution that lands past the 450 ms direct slot start is read as a second old and its burst refused (core/gnss/README.md). ABSENT while PPS is not locked

keys.name: overruns
keys.description: gnss. Times the UART interrupt read bytes from the receiver that its receive ring had no room for, and dropped them (hardware/platform/zephyr/io.h): a service pass that stalled longer than the ring holds at the port's rate

keys.name: identified
keys.description: gnss. The receiver answered the $PCAS06 handshake and named itself. False means an unidentified part, still configured, but a $PCAS dialect we cannot confirm

keys.name: firmware
keys.description: gnss. The receiver's own firmware banner, at most 23 characters of printable ASCII, e.g. URANUS5,V5.1.0.0. Empty when it never introduced itself

keys.name: reject
keys.description: gnss. Why the last solution was not accepted as a fix (core/gnss/validity.h). A named cause, because every one of these has been a support case in one of the reference projects

keys.name: rejected
keys.description: gnss. Solutions refused since boot, one event per run of the same reason

keys.name: residual_m
keys.description: gnss. The extrapolation residual in metres, saturating at 65535: the model the transmitter applies, run over the interval that just elapsed and measured against the fix that closed it. ABSENT rather than zero when there is no pair of consecutive fixes to measure, because 0 m is what a perfect prediction reports.

keys.name: cell_mv
keys.description: power. The battery reading in millivolts, after the per-unit trim (settings.battery_offset_mv): the cell when battery_valid, otherwise what the divider last read, 0 when the ADC gave nothing.

keys.name: percent
keys.description: power. State of charge from the same reading, on the discharge curve, 0 to 100. 0 unless battery_valid

keys.name: battery_valid
keys.description: power. Whether cell_mv is the cell. False with no divider, on a reading outside 1800 to 4700 mV, and on the cable, where the divider reads the USB rail.

keys.name: charging
keys.description: power. The cable is in. No pin says when the charge ends, so a full cell on the cable still reads true

keys.name: power_level
keys.description: power. What core/power's cutoff rule made of the same samples: low about 12%, critical about 5%, flat the device taking itself down, unknown no believable reading yet. The console prints OK, LOW, CRITICAL, FLAT and --.

keys.name: supply_warnings
keys.description: power. Times the nRF52840's power-failure comparator (POFCON) has fired. Any at all on a healthy cell is a supply problem or a threshold set too high, and both are bench work

keys.name: implausible
keys.description: power. Readings the gauge refused: at or under 1800 mV, an unpopulated or unconnected divider rather than a flat cell, or over 4700 mV, which no 4.2 V cell reaches and a rail does. On the cable or off it. cell_mv holds the last one while battery_valid is false

keys.name: die_temperature_c
keys.description: power. Die temperature from -50 to 125 in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. ABSENT rather than zero when no reading exists, because 0.0 C is a plausible hangar morning. Same key and same value as the status reply's.

keys.name: charge
keys.description: power. Whether the die temperature allows the cell to charge (core/power/charging.h): too_cold under 5.0 C, too_hot over 60.0 C, ok between, against LilyGO's 0 to 60 C window with the die's own warmth as the margin at the cold end. Judged only on the cable with a die reading, and ABSENT otherwise, so unknown never travels. The console prints OK, COLD and HOT

keys.name: charge_warnings
keys.description: power. Times the charge condition changed into too_cold or too_hot (products/skyblip_go/services/power.cpp): a cable left in a cold cockpit is one warning, not one a pass

frames.description: The image's state and what an install needs, asked with the bare command and pushed to a connection when it comes up (server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md says how update.js reads it). 57 bytes for a release build at the widest versions scripts/build_image.sh lets through, 59 for a development build.

keys.name: image
keys.description: What became of the last install: confirmed, probation (running, not yet confirmed), reverted (started and never confirmed itself, so the bootloader swapped the old one back) or refused (never started)

keys.name: from
keys.description: The version the last install replaced, as dfu writes it, 0.3.0+1234. Present unless image is confirmed

keys.name: to
keys.description: The version the last install brought, as dfu writes it. Present unless image is confirmed

keys.name: settings
keys.description: What the settings in use fell back to at boot: prior, the copy written on the way into a swap, or defaults (products/skyblip_go/README.md). Absent when they loaded as stored

keys.name: swap_powered
keys.description: The cell allows the flash writes an install needs, by the settings write rule (core/power/cutoff.h)

keys.name: imu
keys.description: What the sensor hub's partition holds: none (no hub answered), missing, corrupt, unreadable (the external flash did not answer), writing (a full image is writing it now, up to a minute) or held

keys.name: imu_digest
keys.description: The first eight bytes of the verified hub blob's SHA-256, present when imu is held

keys.name: downgrade
keys.description: Present and true on a development unit, which accepts an image older than the running one

keys.name: key
keys.description: The first four bytes of the hash of the signing key the bootloader trusts, as imgtool writes it in the image's KEYHASH TLV. Absent when the unit cannot read it

frames.description: Host to unit: asks to install the image of version. The unit answers confirm_dfu and asks on its glass, naming the version, and two presses open a ten-minute upload window for MCUmgr, on the ground only (server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md).

keys.name: version
keys.description: The image's version as read off its header, 0.2.0+15. Absent is refused no_version, and on a release unit a version older than the running one older

frames.description: Host to unit: asks to enter the UF2 bootloader. The unit answers confirm_recovery and asks on its glass, and two presses answer recovery and hand the unit to the bootloader, a USB drive named TECHOBOOT (products/skyblip_go/README.md).
Host to unit: asks to switch the unit off. The unit answers confirm_power_off and asks on its glass, and two presses answer power_off.

Opens an activation session (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json says what each signature covers). The host asks with the bare command, the unit draws a fresh Nu, which replaces any it held, and answers it with the id of the server key it trusts, so the server knows which of its keys to sign with: 27 bytes, answered small_mtu instead on a link that cannot carry it. The nonce dies when unlock uses it, when the link of the session that holds the claim drops, or after ten minutes. Refused keyless by a unit that has no key of its own, could not draw a nonce or cannot read its running version. A unit that lacks a required part, the barometer, shows its refusal page and does not advertise at all, so it cannot be activated. An activated unit refuses challenge, register and unlock as in_flight unless it is on the ground.

keys.name: nonce
keys.description: Nu, 16 random bytes from the hardware RNG, used once

keys.name: server_key_id
keys.description: The id of the server key the firmware is built to trust, the first four bytes of the SHA-256 of its raw 32-byte public key: every device build trusts skyblip.eu's server key (firmware/keys/server.pub), the host suite, the simulator and a local server the public test key of schemas/activation.v1.vectors.json

frames.description: Host to unit, 88 bytes. The unit checks R with the key it trusts and the nonce of this session, then asks on its glass under confirm_register. Two presses answer the registration frame, one press cancelled, thirty seconds expired. On a unit not yet activated the prompt stands whatever the flight state: it is silent, and indoors it has no fix to be on the ground by. An activated unit asks only on the ground, and a take-off cancels the prompt. Refusals: no_session (no live nonce), bad_signature, keyless, small_mtu (the link cannot carry the registration frame in one notification), in_flight (an activated unit off the ground).

keys.name: server_nonce
keys.description: Ns, the server's 16 random bytes, used once

keys.name: signature
keys.description: R, the server's Ed25519 signature over the register message, 'skyblip:register:v1' || Nu || Ns

frames.description: Unit to host after the two presses that answer register, at most 138 bytes in one notification, which an iPhone's 182-byte payload carries. The browser posts its keys to /activation/registrations as they are, byte strings in hexadecimal (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json).

keys.name: device_id
keys.description: DEVICEID, the eight bytes of FICR DEVICEID[1] then DEVICEID[0], each big-endian

keys.name: public_key
keys.description: Pd, the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key of the unit, from its seed in UICR CUSTOMER

keys.name: version
keys.description: The running image, as the dfu command writes it, 0.3.0+1234: at most 23 characters of 0-9, A-Z, a-z, '.', '+' and '-'

keys.name: server_key_id
keys.description: The id of the server key the unit trusts, as in the challenge reply

keys.name: release
keys.description: The unit runs a release build, from a v* tag and the production image key, rather than a development build. Only told to the server, which keeps it beside the key: the air shows no difference, a development unit being a real aircraft with a real serial

keys.name: signature
keys.description: S, the unit's Ed25519 signature over the registration message (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json)

frames.description: Host to unit, at most 74 bytes, carrying what the server answered the registration with. The unit stores serial, Nu and U in its identity page only if U verifies with the key it trusts over its own DEVICEID, its current Pd, the serial and the nonce of this session, then answers acknowledgement with reason unlock and uses the serial from then on. The nonce is spent either way. Refusals: no_session, bad_signature (serial 0 included), flash (the identity page could not be written), low_power (the cell cannot take a flash write), in_flight (an activated unit off the ground).

keys.name: serial
keys.description: Assigned densely by the server, from 1 to 65535: serial 0 would put 0x000000 on the air, which decoders read as no address. The ADS-L address is the manufacturer prefix 0x00 followed by these 16 bits, under address mapping table 58

keys.name: signature
keys.description: U, the server's Ed25519 signature over the unlock message, 'skyblip:unlock:v1' || DEVICEID || Pd || serial as two bytes big-endian || Nu

frames.description: Host to unit on the log endpoint: without index, how many sessions the store holds, answered by a log frame, and with index, that session's entry, answered by a session frame (firmware/core/comms/README.md, The log dialect).

keys.name: log
keys.description: Which store the command addresses: flights, or diagnostics. Absent is flights, and a code that is neither is refused unknown_log

keys.name: index
keys.description: The entry to describe, from 0. Past the last one is refused no_session

frames.description: Host to unit on the log endpoint: asks for count chunks of session from record from, answered back to back by chunk frames. A chunk carries as many whole records as the asking link's payload holds, six at 182 bytes, nine at 244 and nineteen at 495. A link that cannot carry one record is answered small_mtu.

keys.name: log
keys.description: Which store the command addresses: flights, or diagnostics. Absent is flights, and a code that is neither is refused unknown_log

keys.name: session
keys.description: The session to read, by its id as a session frame names it

keys.name: from
keys.description: The record to start at, absent meaning 0

keys.name: count
keys.description: Chunks to send back to back, absent meaning 1, clamped to 1 to 8 (kMaxLogReadChunks)

frames.description: Host to unit on the log endpoint: asks to erase the store. The unit answers confirm_erase_log and asks on its glass, and two presses answer erase_log. The diagnostics store, which is recycled rather than erased, is refused flights_only.

keys.name: log
keys.description: Which store the command addresses: flights, or diagnostics. Absent is flights, and a code that is neither is refused unknown_log

frames.description: Unit to host on the log endpoint: the acknowledgement of a log command, and the answer to list without an index.

keys.name: log
keys.description: The store this reply is about: diagnostics on every diagnostics reply, absent for flights, so two fetches on one link never misfile a chunk

keys.name: acknowledge
keys.description: The command was carried out. False is a refusal named by reason

keys.name: reason
keys.description: Why a log command was refused or what it did, from the enumeration every frame shares

keys.name: sessions
keys.description: How many sessions the store's index offers, on the answer to list

keys.name: truncated
keys.description: On the answer to list, the partition holds more sessions than the index offers

frames.description: Unit to host on the log endpoint: one entry of the store's index, the answer to list with an index. An entry of 256 records or more does not fit the 20 bytes of a link that never exchanged its MTU.

keys.name: log
keys.description: The store this reply is about: diagnostics on every diagnostics reply, absent for flights, so two fetches on one link never misfile a chunk

keys.name: index
keys.description: The entry this is, from 0

keys.name: of
keys.description: How many entries the index holds

keys.name: session
keys.description: The session's id, its opening UTC second: its name, and the base every one of its records is timed against

keys.name: records
keys.description: Records the session holds

keys.name: closed
keys.description: The session was closed. False means the log stops where the power did, and a reader says so rather than present a cut flight as whole

keys.name: truncated
keys.description: The session opened in a sector the ring recycled since, so what is left is a suffix renumbered from record 0, not the whole run

frames.description: Unit to host on the log endpoint: records of one session, an answer to read. Each chunk carries the index it starts at, so the next read is the acknowledgement and asking again from the last index kept is the whole recovery.

keys.name: log
keys.description: The store this reply is about: diagnostics on every diagnostics reply, absent for flights, so two fetches on one link never misfile a chunk

keys.name: session
keys.description: The session these records belong to

keys.name: from
keys.description: The index of the first record in records

keys.name: ends_session
keys.description: This chunk holds the session's last record, and no other chunk of a window says so

keys.name: records
keys.description: Whole records, 24 bytes each as the flash holds them, CRC and all, so the host checks each against the checksum the flash wrote. Their count is the length over 24

frames.description: Host to unit: asks for a cold start of the GNSS receiver. The unit answers confirm_gnss_cold_start and asks on its glass, and two presses answer gnss_cold_start and restart the receiver cold.

Host to unit, proposed: a drawing of the own-ship symbol for one aircraft type, which the ownship editor shows (server/content/ownships/README.md). No firmware reads it yet, so a unit answers unknown_command.

keys.name: aircraft_type
keys.description: The ADS-L aircraft category the drawing is for

keys.name: width
keys.description: The drawing's width in columns, at most 32

keys.name: hot_spot
keys.description: The row the aircraft's position is drawn on

keys.name: rows
keys.description: The drawing, one 32-bit word per row, big-endian, leftmost column in the lowest bit, so its length over 4 is the number of rows
